thread:
Alex: quick sync — we need to decide where precision degradation scoring lives. do we keep it in the runtime or push to a separate eval service?
Maria: +1 to discussing. runtime has low-latency access to token-level signals, but eval service has richer historical context.
Chris: runtime option: immediate failover/on-the-fly precision bump based on short-window drift. service option: aggregated, safer rollouts, but higher decision latency.
Sasha: risk: if runtime owns it, we bloat runtime surface area and couple quant policy to scheduling. if service owns it, we need a clear sync API for per-request signals.
Alex: exact tradeoff. also cost: runtime decisions can reduce tokens sent to expensive models faster, lowering cost. but false positives risk quality regressions.
Maria: proposal A: runtime keeps a lightweight heuristic (latency, approx token-confidence) for instant fallbacks; it calls eval service async for confirmation + tuning.
Chris: proposal B: runtime emits rich telemetry and a control-plane job runs rolling decisions; runtime only accepts explicit control toggles (safer).
Sasha: we should define the signal contract now. minimal set: prompt-id, model-variant, rolling-perplexity, token-drop-rate, quant-profile-id, request-latency. anything else?
sam_oncall: add "sampled-responses-s3-path" so eval can rerun locally. we can't send payloads inline for PII reasons.
Maria: good point re PII. control-plane should reference stored samples, not raw prompts. add KMS-signed references.
quant-ci-bot: CI: canary-metric check flaky — per-token perplexity increase > 1.15 AND semantic-similarity drop > 0.08 -> flag.
Alex: ok, decision mechanics: 1) runtime uses heuristic to toggle to safer quant-profile (e.g., from fp8->int8->int4 degrade path) per-request; 2) telemetry piped to eval service for aggregate scoring; 3) if eval service flags sustained degradation, control-plane issues model-profile pin/rollback.
Chris: edge cases: streaming responses where early tokens look fine but later degrade. heuristic needs to look at suffix-perplexity too. maybe sliding-window of last 64 tokens.
Sasha: interface detail: add header X-Quant-Decision: <heuristic|control> so ops can trace why a request degraded. also surface decision-reason in trace UI.
Maria: rollout/canary: start with a single customer route, synthetic prompts, and live-sampled low-traffic routes. automated rollback on N minutes of failure. define SLOs for "meaningful-perf" (latency + quality).
Alex: can we encode quant profiles as immutable artifacts (sha256) and store them in model registry? runtime just references artifact id. makes rollbacks deterministic.
Chris: yes. and artifact should include expected degradation bounds per eval set. control-plane compares actual vs expected.
sam_oncall: ops ask: how to debug a noisy false positive? need a fast dump endpoint: /debug/trace/<req-id> that includes heuristics, cached kv, profile id, and pointers to sampled response.
Sasha: security: debug endpoint must be RBAC-controlled and audit-logged.
Maria: performance question: how expensive is a runtime check? we should keep heuristic O(1) memops per token. no full model pass. maybe use cached embedding approx or LM logits-sidecar?
Chris: practical approach: precompute small "quality sketch" per request using the existing kv-cache logits (mean logit margin). that's cheap. runtime exposes that sketch.
Alex: next steps: Sasha to sketch signal contract + header names, Chris to prototype runtime heuristic (quick sketch code + perf numbers), Maria to spec eval service aggregate checks and canary rules, sam_oncall to spec debug endpoint + RBAC.
Sasha: I'll drop a short RFC snippet. won't be long.
Chris: I'll prototype using the local test harness, aim for microbench numbers by EOD Thursday.
Maria: I'll write canary playbook bullets and threshold defaults.
sam_oncall: I'll mock the debug endpoint and an RBAC policy.
quant-ci-bot: Action items added to board: #Q-342, #Q-343, #Q-344.
Alex: thanks. one more: document the fallback ladder and exposure to cost analytics so product can see impact.
Maria: noted. I'll add cost delta metric per-profile to the canary dashboard.
Alex: cool. if nobody objects, we'll run this as the working plan. :thumbsup:
Chris: no objections from me.
Sasha: fine by me.
Maria: looks good.
Alex: closing thread, will ping when RFC snippet lands.
